#### Goal:
Developing working knowledge of linear models in R: fitting them, reading diagnostic plots, and judging when a model is (or is not) correctly specified.


#### sample Simulation foundations on a linear and quadratic  terms.
general approach;

- Create the simulated dataset.
- Fit the three linear models described above.
- Use the predict() function to obtain observed and fitted values.
- Use the resid() function to obtain residual values.
- Plot the observed and fitted data points, as well as the residual values.


```{r}

#Starting with default variables to assess association between x and y
#General f(x) = 20 + 10*x + 5x^2 to test with models.
# + noise = rnorm(100, 0, 1.5)
x=1:20 
y = 20+10*1:20+5*(1:20)^2+rnorm(20,0,200)
dfr <- data.frame(x , y)

fx <-  20 + 10*x + 5*x^2  # function without noise
fxn <- 20+10*1:20+5*(1:20)^2+rnorm(20,0,200) # function + noise



#model 1; m1 :  intercept only (y~1) ; 

m1 <-  lm( y~1 , data = dfr)
summary(m1)
#model 2; m2 : intercept and slope (y~x)

m2 <- lm(y~x , data = dfr)
summary(m2)
#model 3, m3 = intercept, slope, and curvature,quadratic term x^2 #(y~x+I(x^2)).

m3 <- lm( y~x + I(x^2) , data = dfr)
summary(m3)

#----predicting observed values
m1.obs <- predict(m1)
m2.obs <- predict(m1)
m3.obs <- predict(m1)

#---- obtaining residuals values

m1.resid <- resid(m1)
m2.resid <- resid(m2)
m3.resid <- resid(m3)

# plotting observed and fitted + residuals

for (i in 1:3) {
  lms <- list(m1, m2, m3)[[i]]          # model i
  plot(dfr$x, dfr$y, pch = 19,
       xlab = "x", ylab = "y",
       main = c("(1) y ~ 1", "(2) y ~ x", "(3) y ~ x + I(x^2)")[i])
  lines(dfr$x, fx, lty = 2, col = "grey50")        # truth
  points(dfr$x, predict(lms), col = "red", pch = 20) # fitted pts
  lines(dfr$x, predict(lms), col = "red")            # fitted shape
}



for (i in 1:3) {
  lms<- list(m1, m2, m3)[[i]]
  plot(fitted(lms), resid(lms), pch = 19,
       xlab = "Fitted values", ylab = "Residuals",
       main = c("(1) y ~ 1", "(2) y ~ x", "(3) y ~ x + I(x^2)")[i])
  abline(h = 0, lty = 2, col = "red")
  lines(lowess(fitted(lms), resid(lms)), col = "blue", lwd = 2)
}


```
